title.narrative: WGG- Feminist Leadership and Mentorship in Bangladesh

description.narrative: The objective of the strategy is to destabilise these structures by ensuring new women leaders are represented in policy and decision making spaces as well in convenings and conversations.

The program strategy aims to capacitate new women leaders, including WWDs and young women, on feminist leadership to build inclusive movements and alliances. The program recognises power structures, both visible and hidden, that exist within movements.

sector.narrative: Support for feminist, women-led and women's rights organisations and movements, and institutions (governmental and non-govermental) at all levels to enhance their effectiveness, influence and substainability (activities and core-funding). These organisations exist to bring about transformative change for gender equality and/or the rights of women and girls in developing countries. Their activities include agenda-setting, advocacy, policy dialogue, capacity development, awareness raising and prevention, service provision, conflict-prevention and peacebuilding, research, organising, and alliance and network building

Training to Girls and Women with disabilities Sexual and Gender-Based Violence, and other training activities

4 YLs have gained increased knowledge and capacity to participate and engage in local level advocacy on gender equality and elimination of SGBV. One in Sylhet, two in Dhaka, one in Bandarban have been actively taking part in community-level as well as regional and national level advocacy initiatives engaging with other rights based organizations and networks.Income-generating materials distribution program aimed at empowering women with disabilities from Dalit and Minority communities in the tea gardens of Sreemangal. This initiative was part of “Women Gaining Ground" project, funded by IWRAW Asia Pacific, and technically supported by the Moulovibazar Cha Jonogosti Adibasi Front. A total of 12 women with disabilities from the tea gardens of Sreemangal were selected for this program.
Training to Girls and Women with disabilities Sexual and Gender-Based Violence, and other training activities

8 young leaders (YLs) took part in two residential workshops from Bonhishikha on feminist leadership and mentoring—one in June and the other in October—during which their leadership skills were developed in order to position them for active political engagement. Through WDDF, In Khulna district, 29 women and girls with disabilities took part in a two-day training on SGBV and political participation with Disabled People's Organisation(DPO) Representative Women and Girls With Disabilitiess. Another total of 48 girls and women with disabilities got help for economic empowerment under feminist leadership and mentoring. The format of the 5-part training was to create a commitment to preventing SGBV and, if necessary, providing legal aid.

Training to Girls and Women with disabilities Sexual and Gender-Based Violence, and other training activities

In 2023 partner conducted one leadership building training A total of 25 Young Women and Women with Disabilities Individuals and collectives participated in the training program which resulted in increased knowledge resources, tools and capacities of the participants. In 2023, 20 YLs from one partner's program joined the WGG programme, making the total number of participants 28 in the current year. All the YLs participated in two residential workshops on Feminist Leadership in 2023, followed by a monthly thematic learning session and mentoring sessions through which their leadership and organising capacity is being built to prepare them for active political participation.

Young Women & Women with Disabilities participating in political processes/

The 28 Young Leaders are able to demonstrate their skills for negotiations, awareness raising and active participation in discourses around similar issues in different political, civic and social spaces. Some of them engaged with local police for mass campaign on ensuring privacy and safeguarding from sexual harassment of local indigenous women. Some YLs did advocacy with local political leader and elites helped support hijras (trans persons) 'reintegrate in their community.
